reserved_clusters.title: Pursuit of spatial justice in architecture

source_candidates.label: Edward W. Soja, Seeking Spatial Justice, University of Minnesota Press
source_candidates.locator: web.open University of Minnesota Press lines 104-122 and 147-153 for bibliographic data, spatial justice summary, and source boundary.

source_candidates.label: PRC Board of Architecture, IRR of RA 9266, Theory of Architecture syllabus
source_candidates.locator: web.open RA 9266 IRR lines 659-682 for BLEA subjects and Theory of Architecture sociocultural/technological trends.

source_candidates.label: RA 9266 Board Law, scope of architecture practice for site, housing, community architecture, and quality of life
source_candidates.locator: web.open PRC Board Law lines 50-87 for site analysis, housing design, community architecture, space planning, building programming, and quality-of-life practice scope.

source_candidates.label: PRC Resolution No. 05, Series of 2011, BLEA Tables of Specifications
source_candidates.locator: web.open Supreme Court E-Library lines 43-80 and 109 for BLEA subject scope, TOS authority, and 2012-and-after applicability.

source_candidates.label: POLITesi, Resilient Edges: Metro Manila flood risk assessment
source_candidates.locator: web.open POLITesi lines 19-23 and 36-41 for Metro Manila flooding, informal settlements, spatial morphology, and community action context.

source_candidates.label: PRC CPDAS provider page for United Architects of the Philippines: placemaking/community CPD evidence
source_candidates.locator: web.open CPDAS lines 7-29 for UAP provider status and lines 257-263, 291, and 338 for placemaking, community engagement, and socially responsive architecture entries.

included: Spatial justice as a theory that links justice to geography and distribution of resources, services, and access.
Spatial justice as a source-safe Theory of Architecture topic when framed as a sociocultural trend, not as a named BLEA line item.
RA 9266 practice-scope language for site analysis, housing design, community architecture, space planning, building programming, and quality-of-life promotion.
Philippine informal-settlement and flood-risk examples as contextual application only, supported by academic repository evidence.
UAP CPDAS placemaking/community/digital placemaking entries as evidence that inclusive public-space discourse appears in professional development.
excluded: A claim that the BLEA explicitly names spatial justice.
A claim that Soja directly writes about bayanihan or Philippine informal settlements.
General encyclopedia, news, blog, or lifestyle articles as primary authority.
Legal mandates for community land trusts, anti-displacement instruments, or design outcomes not captured in Batch 159 sources.

source_candidates.label: PRC Board of Architecture, IRR of RA 9266, Theory of Architecture syllabus
source_candidates.locator: web.open RA 9266 IRR lines 659-682 for BLEA subjects and Theory of Architecture sociocultural/technological trends.

source_candidates.label: RA 9266 Board Law, scope of architecture practice including architectural computer-aided design
source_candidates.locator: web.open PRC Board Law lines 50-87 for practice scope, coordination, quality of life, and architectural computer-aided design.

source_candidates.label: PRBoA Standards of Professional Practice, SPP Document 206 comprehensive architectural services
source_candidates.locator: web.open SPP lines 1727-1739 and 1740-1789 for comprehensive service categories and architect coordination role.

source_candidates.label: Branko Kolarevic, Architecture in the Digital Age: Design and Manufacturing, NJIT research output record
source_candidates.publisher: New Jersey Institute of Technology / Taylor and Francis bibliographic record
source_candidates.locator: web.open NJIT lines 15-32, 83-91, and 132-136 for bibliographic data and digital technologies changing conception, design, and production.

source_candidates.label: PRC CPDAS provider page for United Architects of the Philippines: BIM, CAD-to-BIM, digital tools, and AI CPD evidence
source_candidates.locator: web.open CPDAS lines 7-29 for UAP provider status, lines 254-256 and 292-296 for CAD/BIM/digital tools, lines 670-676 for AI/BIM entries, and lines 1085-1090 for 2025 BIM and technology-and-innovation entries.

included: Digital architecture as a technological trend within the Theory of Architecture syllabus boundary.
Architectural computer-aided design as explicitly within RA 9266/IRR scope of architecture practice.
Digital technologies changing how buildings are conceived, designed, and produced, supported by an academic bibliographic record for Kolarevic.
UAP CPDAS evidence of BIM, CAD-to-BIM, digital tools, AI, and technology-and-innovation CPD programs.
SPP 206 service categories as the professional service frame across pre-design, design, construction, post-construction, and specialized services.
excluded: A claim that any software vendor, platform, or AI tool is required by the cited regulators or professional bodies.
A claim that digital architecture is a standalone BLEA subject.
A claim that AI outputs, code-compliance automation, or generative design can replace professional judgment.
General encyclopedia, news, blog, or commercial rendering articles as primary authority.
